test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
In the given figure, AB is parallel to EF. ED is parallel to CB and angle APE is 60 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle EQC?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d93771108cb405f29b4c500a4bafb44a4d3c77528fea4e42afe9671b6a0392f5.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given AB || EF, then ∠APE = ∠PEF (Alternate interior angles).

Given ED || CB, then ∠PEF = ∠EQC (Alternate interior angles).

Since ∠APE = 60°, it follows that ∠PEF = 60°.

Therefore, ∠EQC = 60°.

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

AB || EF

ED || CB

∠APE = 60°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b8f28b1063301bd364d5191d3722afc9a6701a5a1e0582b072c7bcc57511f8bd.png] 

Step-by-step calculation:

⇒ Consider line AB parallel to line EF with line ED as the transversal.

⇒ ∠APE and ∠PEF are alternate interior angles.

⇒ ∴ ∠PEF = ∠APE = 60°

⇒ Now, consider line ED parallel to line CB with line EF as the transversal.

⇒ ∠PEF and ∠EQC are alternate interior angles.

⇒ ∴ ∠EQC = ∠PEF = 60°

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Interior Angles

When two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, the pairs of angles on opposite sides of the transversal and between the parallel lines are equal.

Corresponding Angles

Angles in the same relative position at each intersection where a straight line crosses two parallel lines are equal.

Consecutive Interior Angles

Interior angles on the same side of the transversal are supplementary, meaning their sum is 180°.

Parallelogram Property

In a parallelogram formed by two pairs of parallel lines, opposite angles are equal and consecutive angles are supplementary.
